title: Sultan Khan v. State of U.P. and others
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Sunita Agarwal and Sadhna Rani (Thakur), JJ.
disposition: Writ petition dismissed; petitioner relegated to the competent authority under the Electricity Act, 2003 and the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
headnote: A writ seeking correction of an electricity bill dated 9 October 2020 and restoration of supply, after a disconnection notice for unpaid dues and an FIR under section 135 of the Electricity Act, 2003 against the petitioner's son, was dismissed. The Division Bench held that the issues required a factual inquiry and that the consumer had a remedy before the competent authority under the Electricity Act, 2003 and the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
facts: Sultan Khan sought a mandamus to correct an electricity bill dated 9 October 2020 and to restore his supply. The licensee had issued a notice dated 15 October 2020 threatening disconnection for unpaid dues, and an FIR under section 135 of the Electricity Act, 2003 had been lodged against his son. He claimed a valid connection and that the bill was based on incorrect facts. Counsel did not appear on two earlier listings; the Division Bench took up the petition on 8 July 2021 with the licensee's counsel present.

holding_units.holding: Where a consumer seeks a writ of mandamus to correct an electricity bill and restore supply, and the dispute turns on facts including alleged unpaid dues, the High Court will not inquire into the bill: the consumer has a remedy before the competent authority under the Electricity Act, 2003 and the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and the writ petition is dismissed.

principle_tags.application: The Court treated the lis as a billing and reconnection dispute requiring factual inquiry, noted but did not decide the section 135 FIR against the petitioner's son, and dismissed the writ because a competent-authority remedy existed under the Electricity Act, 2003 and the Supply Code, 2005.

not_decided.point: Correctness of the electricity bill dated 9 October 2020
Whether the electricity connection should be restored or reconnected
The first information report under section 135 of the Electricity Act, 2003 against the petitioner's son
not_decided.note: Recorded as background; the Court treated the dispute as one about the bill and did not examine the FIR.
